issues.body: `_on_block` ignores the value captured after the top-level `on:` key and only scans indented following lines. Consequently, valid YAML forms such as `on: workflow_run` and `on: {workflow_run: {types: [completed]}}` produce zero offences even though they declare `workflow_run` without a non-empty `workflows` filter. This contradicts the stated every-trigger invariant and makes the gating check bypassable.
issues.fix_hint: Parse and validate supported scalar/flow forms of the top-level `on` value, preferably with a real YAML parser or a deliberately complete structural parser. Add red self-test fixtures for `on: workflow_run`, `on: [workflow_run]`, and top-level flow mappings with missing or empty `workflows`.
issues.title: Top-level scalar and flow-style `on` declarations bypass the guard

issues.body: The inline-form regex alternation accepts an empty flow list: the first branch rejects `[]`, but the scalar fallback `workflows\s*:\s*[^\s,}]` matches its opening `[`. Running `check_text` on `on:\n  workflow_run: {workflows: []}\n` returns an empty offence list. The block-form equivalent is tested and rejected, so the two syntaxes enforce different semantics.
issues.fix_hint: Replace the ambiguous regex with structural parsing of the inline mapping/list, or ensure the scalar branch cannot consume `[` and explicitly reject empty flow sequences. Add the inline-empty-list case to `_self_test` and require it to red.
issues.title: Inline `workflow_run: {workflows: []}` is incorrectly accepted

verdict.summary: The guard is fail-open for valid YAML trigger forms. Empirical checks against check_text show that it returns no offences for both `on: workflow_run` / top-level flow syntax and `workflow_run: {workflows: []}`. These bypass the exact invariant the new gating check claims to enforce, while the self-test suite omits those cases.
